To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the maximum mass of a hybrid star is reduced by the presence of color superconducting quark phase; and (b) the presence of a color superconducting phase can increase the radius of a hybrid star by 20%.

the existence of color superconducting quarks inside compact stars may explain most of the observational constraints on the masses and radii and that it is possible for a compact star to be made of quarks only, with a mass as large as 3.2 solar masses.

the existence of a color superconducting diquark condensation in compact stars is consistent with the recent observational data on compact stellar objects, and the constraints from these data on masses and radiis of compact stellar objects provide stringent limits on the values of the parameters of the nuclear equation.

the compact stars are very sensitive to the equation of state of the matter in the core.
we have shown that the quark phase is not ruled out by the recent observational data on compact stars, and that the quark matter phase is a very promising candidate for the core of compact stars.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the color superconductivity is an essential ingredient to describe the interior of compact stars, especially for the heaviest stars.
the color superconductivity is an essential ingredient for understanding the structure of compact stellar objects.
